reading.text:
Reading for def:Dissertation.WellPosedness.System.lawToL2 (locked before any Lean is shown).

Paper notion. The paper has no object called "lawToL2". The two notions the name can stand for:
 (A) the law map on L^2 (Lemma A.1 step 2; Def 2.1): Theta |-> Law(Theta), from
     L^2(Omega;H) (or L^2(Omega,F_t;H)) to P_2(H), the push-forward P o Theta^{-1}, which lies in
     P_2(H) since E|Theta|^2 < inf, and which is 1-Lipschitz for W_2 (coupling bound (2.coupling));
     it depends only on the P-a.e. class of Theta;
 (B) a map from a law mu in P_2(H) to an L^2 random variable with that law on some probability
     space (the kernel-representation direction of Remark 2.8 / Kallenberg Lemma 4.22), e.g. used
     to realise W_2 through L^2 couplings.
A faithful Lean definition must be:
 for (A): for an element of the Lean L^2 type, the push-forward of P under (any representative
 of) it, packaged as an element of the P_2(H) type, the second-moment proof coming from L^2
 membership; the H being the paper's H (Hilbert norm, Borel sets).
 for (B): a random variable whose law is exactly mu (for every mu in P_2(H)), square integrable.
In either case no junk: the map must be total and correct on all inputs of its domain.

comparison.text:
Comparison for def:Dissertation.WellPosedness.System.lawToL2.

Lean: lawToL2 mu := mu.mapOfLe measurable_toL2 norm_toL2_le : P2 (TupleL2 ...), i.e. the push-forward
toL2 # mu of a law on the (max-norm) product Tuple to the same space realised with the Hilbert
norm, with the second-moment bound from |toL2 theta| <= 2|theta|. My reading guessed (A) the law map
L^2 -> P_2 or (B) a representation of a law by an L^2 variable; neither is what the unit is. The
paper notion it stands for is the identity of P_2(H): toL2 is the identity of the carrier H
(ofL2 o toL2 = id by rfl), changing only the norm instance from max to Hilbert; so lawToL2 mu is the
same law on H, now in the type whose norm is |.|_H. It is used to put W_2 of the Hilbert norm on
P2WH (instPseudoMetricSpace) and to define w2H.
- does not alter the measure (push-forward along a measurable bijection with measurable inverse,
  the identity on points): OK.
- total, no junk (mapOfLe needs only measurability and the norm bound, both proved). OK.
Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
Representation choice, harmless: the paper has a single P_2(H). The Lean has laws on the max-norm
product (Tuple) and on its Hilbert-norm realisation (TupleL2). lawToL2 moves a law from the first
to the second along toL2, which is the identity on points (ofL2 (toL2 theta) = theta by rfl) and
measurable. So it is the identity of P_2(H) between two encodings of H. The finite second moment
is carried over by |toL2 theta| <= 2 |theta|.

author_review.disagreements:
No substantive disagreement. The review shown records "faithful". I recorded "faithful with
representation choices" because the paper has a single P_2(H). lawToL2 is the identity of P_2(H)
between the two Lean encodings of H (the max-norm product and its Hilbert-norm realisation).
That is a representation step, harmless, and the review describes the same map.
